negative_findings.description: Searches for a Global Payments / Erste Group joint venture covering Hungary returned only the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Romania JV (announced 2015-07-27, closed 2016-06-01) plus a later Croatian extension. Hungary appears instead as a 2014 outsourcing of Erste Bank Hungary's POS network to Global Payments Europe, not as an equity JV.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Hungary-specific Erste/Global Payments JV press release located; Hungarian relationship is an outsourcing/partnership announced Oct 2014 on erstebank.hu.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The corporate structure determines where Hungarian acquiring revenue is booked and therefore which filing to track; assuming a JV would send collection to the wrong disclosure channel.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Hungarian-language Mastercard press room (mastercard.hu/sajtokozlemenyek) surfaced; Hungarian Mastercard announcements appear either on the pan-European English newsroom or only via Hungarian trade press (FinTechZone, Privátbankár, vg.hu).
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungarian Mastercard PR must be collected indirectly from the European newsroom plus HU trade-press mirrors.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Creates a dependency on third-party republication, with attribution and completeness risk for scheme-sourced Hungarian statistics.

negative_findings.description: Euronet's recent 10-K names Hungary only as a processing-centre location and reports the EFT Processing segment in aggregate (47,303 ATMs network-wide, ~29% of consolidated revenue in 2023); no Hungary revenue or ATM-count line item was found in the filings surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungary-level Euronet figures are not in group filings; must be triangulated from the Hungarian statutory accounts and the euronetatms.hu press releases.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations for what the 10-K can and cannot answer, and justifies the e-beszamolo collection path as critical.

negative_findings.description: The Hungarian/English token 'Visa' is heavily polluted by travel-visa content (e.g. Hungary visa requirements pages surfaced in a payments query). Similarly 'Nexi' collides with unrelated brands.
negative_findings.result_summary: Scheme-name queries must be constrained with payments terms (kártya, elfogadás, fizetés, bankkártya) or site-scoped to visa.hu.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Unconstrained scheme-name monitoring will produce a high false-positive rate in any automated collection.

negative_findings.description: No URL in this slice was fetch-verified; all were observed as search-result links only. Worldline's Hungarian media-relations paths in particular are unusually deep and may have rotated.
negative_findings.result_summary: All URLs supplied as hypotheses for the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Deep-path corporate CMS URLs are the most likely to 404 while the section index stays live; verification should fall back to section indexes.

coverage_gaps.description: No source located for card-scheme domestic interchange fee schedules published for Hungary (Mastercard/Visa country interchange PDFs), which is where the regulated economics of Hungarian acquiring is actually stated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Targeted search on 'Mastercard interchange Hungary domestic fee schedule' and 'Visa Hungary hazai bankközi jutalék' plus scheme fee-disclosure subdomains; likely PDF-only.

coverage_gaps.description: Processor actors with Hungarian back-office/processing operations beyond the named five were not explored (e.g. FIS/Worldpay, Diebold Nixdorf, ACI, Tietoevry, and card personalisation/processing bureaus with Budapest sites).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Second pass mapping Budapest-based processing/service-centre footprints of listed payment technology vendors via their 10-K/annual report property sections and Hungarian job postings.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian-language terminology for the acquiring/processing layer was harvested (kártyaelfogadás, elfogadóhely, elfogadói hálózat, elfogadói üzletág, POS terminál, bankkártya-elfogadás, sajtóközlemény, éves beszámoló) but no Hungarian term set was established for scheme-side concepts such as interchange, scheme fees or tokenisation.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the missing glossary from MNB payment-systems reports and scheme Hungarian fee documents (bankközi jutalék, kereskedői jutalék/MSC, tranzakciós illeték) before the next collection run.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival/wayback strategy captured for the corporate press rooms in this cell, which routinely reorganise URLs (Visa.hu numeric slugs, Worldline deep paths, SIX legacy estate).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Register the key press-room indexes with a snapshot service and store both canonical and archived URLs for every collected item.

coverage_gaps.description: Exact Hungarian legal-entity names and registration numbers were confirmed only for Nexi Hungary Zrt. and Visa Europe (Hungary) Kft.; the Worldline/SIX and Global Payments Hungarian entities were not pinned down, blocking a complete e-beszamolo pull.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve remaining entities via OPTEN/cegjegyzek preview pages and the companies' own Hungarian imprint (impresszum/jogi nyilatkozat) pages before running the statutory-accounts collection.

brief: Hungarian disclosure by the scheme/acquirer/processor layer splits cleanly into three tiers: English-language regulated filings of listed parents (Euronet, Global Payments, Worldline, Nexi, Visa/Mastercard) that name Hungary only in passing; Hungarian-language corporate press rooms of the local operating arms (euronetatms.hu, visa.hu, globalpayments.com/hu-hu, worldline.com/hu-hu, erstebank.hu) that carry the real operational detail; and the statutory accounts on the Ministry of Justice e-beszamolo portal, which is the only official route to Hungary-level revenue for actors that never break the country out. Euronet is the standout: founded as a Hungarian company, still running a Budapest processing centre, and with a 30-year filing trail in EDGAR. The acquiring structure is an outsourcing relationship (Erste Bank Hungary to Global Payments Europe since 2014) rather than the CEE equity JV that covers Czechia/Slovakia/Romania, so collection must target the Hungarian bank's press room alongside the acquirer's. The main weaknesses are the absence of a Hungarian Mastercard press room, no located Hungarian domestic interchange schedules, and unresolved legal-entity identifiers for the Worldline and Global Payments Hungarian arms.
